tema: Evaluates the diagnostic performance of serum GDF-15 in distinguishing primary mitochondrial myopathy (PMM) from CFS in patients with fatigue and exercise intolerance.
diseno: Diagnostic study in 34 adults with fatigue and exercise intolerance: 7 with PMM, 22 with CFS and 5 with other non-mitochondrial disorders; GDF-15 measurement and ROC curve analysis.
hallazgos: GDF-15 discriminated accurately between PMM and CFS (AUC=0.95) and between PMM and fatigue from other non-mitochondrial disorders (AUC=0.94).
conclusion: GDF-15 is a useful serum biomarker for deciding which patients with fatigue require further studies to rule out mitochondrial disease, avoiding unnecessary tests.
triangulacion: Full coherence among the three sources. GDF-15 is raised as a differential diagnosis tool, not as a CFS marker; the sample is small.

tema: Evaluates sex differences in fatigue, function and autonomic recovery after a low-load exercise protocol in ME/CFS.
diseno: Pilot study with 22 women and 15 men with ME/CFS and 14 controls; two six-minute walk tests (days 8 and 9); 15 daily assessments of fatigue, function and cardiac monitoring (HRV).
hallazgos: Patients showed no significant HRV changes; HR fell in men between days 14 and 15. Women increased fatigue after the first walk and then it decreased; men reduced work limitation; controls reduced HRV.
conclusion: It was not confirmed that women recover more slowly than men; a test more sensitive to exertion may be required to document prolonged post-exertional abnormalities.
triangulacion: Abstract and keywords are consistent. The conclusions (discussion with noise from figure legends) reiterate the need for a more demanding test and point out opposing fatigue trends between groups.

tema: Pilot study evaluating sex-dependent transcriptional changes in response to an exercise challenge in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with RNA-Seq in 33 ME/CFS patients (20 women, 13 men) and 34 matched controls (20 women, 14 men), before, during and after an exercise challenge designed to provoke PEM.
hallazgos: In men with ME/CFS, exertion activated immune signalling pathways (including IL-12) and NK cell cytotoxicity, and in recovery changes in signals such as IL-1β; in women there were not enough changes to meet differential expression criteria, although there were alterations in cellular stress networks, herpesvirus response and NF-κB signalling.
conclusion: The results delineate differences between men and women in the transcriptomic effect of exercise and recovery; larger cohorts, multi-omic integration and standardized PEM measures are required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on sex differences, PEM and differential gene expression; the PDF conclusions add limitations and the difficulty of measuring PEM because of its subjective nature.

tema: Reviews the microglial and immuno-inflammatory mechanisms shared between depression and CFS and their comorbidity.
diseno: Narrative review of clinical and preclinical studies (including stress models in mice). No sample stated.
hallazgos: A systemic pro-inflammatory state explains fatigue and physiosomatic symptoms in depression; in CFS, immune activation is associated with greater depressive severity. Animal data show greater microglial activation by stress in females, with no direct evidence in CFS.
conclusion: Shared immuno-inflammatory pathways and activated microglia could underpin depression-CFS comorbidity and be therapeutic targets, as well as helping to understand sex differences.
triangulacion: Keywords, opening text (which only contains the accepted manuscript header) and conclusions are consistent; the abstract provides no content, and the conclusions acknowledge that there is no direct evidence of microglial dimorphism in CFS.

tema: Examines the association between silicone breast implants and depression, fibromyalgia and CFS in a rheumatology practice.
diseno: Retrospective case-control study with medical records (Royal Adelaide Hospital, 2000-2017); 30 women with implants and controls with systemic sclerosis and SLE matched 3:1 for age and sex.
hallazgos: Twelve cases had depression, six fibromyalgia and three CFS; implant rupture was not associated. No differences versus SLE; versus systemic sclerosis there was more fibromyalgia and/or CFS (20.0% versus 2.2%; p = 0.01).
conclusion: Fibromyalgia and CFS are more frequent in patients with implants than in controls with systemic sclerosis, but not than in SLE; prospective studies are required.
triangulacion: Coherence in focus. The conclusions (discussion) are more cautious: they point out as a confounder the high baseline prevalence of fibromyalgia and CFS in the rheumatological population and the lack of autoantibody data.

tema: Objectively evaluates autonomic function in post-COVID condition (PCC) and in non-COVID ME/CFS to check whether they share abnormalities.
diseno: Case-control study with 34 ME/CFS patients, 29 with PCC and 32 healthy controls; ECG and continuous digital blood pressure (Penaz method, spiroarteriocardiorhythmography); HRV and blood pressure variability at rest and with controlled breathing; baroreflex sensitivity.
hallazgos: Total power, LF and HF of RR intervals and baroreflex sensitivity were lower in PCC and ME/CFS than in controls; with slow breathing HRV normalized in PCC but not in ME/CFS. HRV, pressure variability and baroreflex correlated with fatigue, not with anxiety or depression (HADS); diagnostic predictive models for ME/CFS were developed.
conclusion: ME/CFS and PCC show a similar pattern of HRV and baroreflex failure with signs of pathological acceleration of age-dependent dysautonomia.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions come from the structured abstract and reproduce it. The difference during slow breathing qualifies the 'similarity' of the title.

tema: Conceptualizes loneliness and social isolation in people with ME, as a chronic and contested illness.
diseno: Sociological qualitative analysis of 42 accounts from people with ME.
hallazgos: Proposes two concepts: necessary social isolation (symptoms restrict social life) and forced loneliness (stigma and contested illness lead to withdrawal and rejection). Identifies three themes: spatio-temporal restriction, communicative alienation and discredit, in a self-reinforcing cycle.
conclusion: The stigmatization of ME aggravates loneliness and marginalizes its needs; interventions must prioritize meaningful, empathic relationships over increasing social contacts.
triangulacion: High coherence among the three sources; the PDF conclusions add intervention recommendations not present in the abstract (they include publisher download noise).

tema: Examines physiological responses to a graded exercise test in CFS and subclassifies patients by degree of disability.
diseno: Study with CPET in 189 CFS patients assigned to four disability categories (none, mild, moderate, severe) according to AMA guidelines; MANOVA.
hallazgos: There were differences between levels in % of predicted VO2 and peak HR; peak systolic BP of the moderate and severe groups differed from the rest, with lower values in the most affected. Peak VO2 was below predicted in all groups and women came closer to their predicted value than men.
conclusion: Functional capacity varies greatly despite a common diagnosis; stratifying by function allows responses to be interpreted better and could help differentiate subgroups.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions add that the HR and BP profiles in the most affected are compatible with cardiac autonomic dysfunction, without ruling out other causes.

tema: Evaluates whether the disease course allows ME/CFS patients to be subclassified according to symptoms, function and energy expenditure.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with 541 participants; DSQ, SF-36 and energy expenditure measures compared between self-described trajectories.
hallazgos: Courses: fluctuating (59.7%), steadily worsening (15.9%), persistent (14.1%), relapse-remission (8.5%) and steadily improving (1.9%). They were associated with significant differences in DSQ domains, SF-36 subscales and energy expenditure.
conclusion: Subclassifying by disease course is a promising method for creating more homogeneous groups and improving research and treatment.
triangulacion: High coherence among keywords, abstract and conclusions; the latter describe the results as preliminary, a nuance of caution.

tema: Reviews the evidence for immunometabolic dysfunction in T and NK cells in ME/CFS and whether they reflect states of anergy, exhaustion or senescence.
diseno: Narrative review of the immunometabolic literature in ME/CFS, compared with chronic viral infections. No sample stated.
hallazgos: CD8+ T cell exhaustion appears as a probable candidate, whereas the state of CD4+ T cells and NK cells remains unclear. There are indications that metabolic dysfunction partly drives dysfunctional immune states; heterogeneity could be due to different phases of the disease and cytokine fluctuations.
conclusion: The similarity with chronic viral infections (hypometabolic state and lower effector function) suggests dysfunctional states in T and NK cells, consistent with the chronic viral disease hypothesis.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions add nuances about longitudinal variability and disease duration as an explanation for contradictory results.

tema: Identifies groups (clusters) of ME/CFS patients according to symptom frequency and severity.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with 337 members of the Dutch ME/CFS Foundation (online DSQ-2); self-organizing maps (SOM); validation in an additional sample of 252.
hallazgos: 45 clusters were identified, 13 with 10 or more patients; fatigue and PEM were present in all, but they differed in severity and frequency pattern and in clinical characteristics. 11% were not classified; the pattern was reproduced in the validation sample.
conclusion: There are subgroups of patients with similar symptom patterns, confirmed in an independent sample, useful for developing tailored treatments.
triangulacion: High coherence; the PDF conclusions repeat the abstract and add the need to relate clusters to quality of life and functioning.

tema: Systematic review and meta-analysis to delineate the neuropsychological profile of ME/CFS.
diseno: Review according to PRISMA and MOOSE of 764 studies (1988-2019) in PubMed Central and Clarivate, with meta-analysis.
hallazgos: Immediate visuospatial memory (g = -0.55), reading speed (g = -0.82) and graphic gesture (g = -0.59) are affected, with difficulties in verbal and visual episodic memory and low attentional efficiency; executive functions are little or not at all affected and instrumental ones preserved.
conclusion: The cognitive profile is complex and heterogeneous and requires complete neuropsychological assessment; the authors suggest adapted cognitive remediation and considering fatigue, pain and mood.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on visuospatial memory, reading speed and episodic memory; the conclusions (from the discussion) add reaction time and psychosocial impact.

tema: Evaluates systemic hyperalgesia in women with Gulf War illness, CFS and fibromyalgia.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in 920 women classified by Kansas, Fukuda 1994 and ACR 1990 criteria; dolorimetry at 18 tender points; ROC curves and symptom questionnaires.
hallazgos: Mean pain threshold: Gulf War 2.9 kg, CFS/FM 3.1 kg, FM 3.9 kg and CFS 5.8 kg versus 7.2 kg in controls (p < 0.0001). ROC thresholds: 4.0 kg for Gulf War and CFS/FM, 4.5 kg for FM and 6.0 kg for CFS. Dolorimetry correlated with symptoms only in Gulf War illness.
conclusion: All three conditions show systemic hyperalgesia; pressure sensitivity could complement the diagnostic criteria and help in the diagnosis of CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree; the conclusions text (discussion) actually corresponds to methods and limitations (convenience samples, incomplete questionnaires), which qualifies the robustness of the results.

tema: Profiles antibody responses against microbiota and viral antigens in severe ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study in patients with severe ME/CFS and healthy controls, using a library of 244,000 phage-displayed variants (PhIP-Seq) and machine learning algorithms. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Patients showed distinct epitope repertoires against flagellins from Lachnospiraceae bacteria. Models trained with these data provided additional information to standard blood analyses and improved molecular diagnosis.
conclusion: The results point to an involvement of the microbiota-immune system axis in ME/CFS and lay the groundwork for comparison with inflammatory bowel disease and post-COVID syndrome.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent. The conclusions text is only methodological noise (statistics, supplementary material), so it provides no triangulation.

tema: Describes a case of systemic exertion intolerance disease (SEID) associated with neuroendocrine dysfunction and cortical atrophy.
diseno: Case report following CARE guidelines of a patient with 5 years of nonspecific symptoms diagnosed with SEID.
hallazgos: Low serum TSH and ACTH, 24-h urinary cortisol almost double the upper limit and significant cortical atrophy on CT were detected; low-dose modafinil, together with a non-pharmacological approach, improved the clinical course.
conclusion: The diagnosis and treatment of SEID are challenging; family doctors must be familiar with it, and complementary imaging and endocrine axis studies are recommended.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The keywords focus on neuroendocrine findings and modafinil, not on exercise; the conclusions add mechanistic proposals about modafinil of a speculative nature.

tema: Examines whether sleep quality, daytime naps, patient characteristics and mood predict fatigue, daytime sleepiness and cognitive functioning in CFS.
diseno: Observational study with 118 adults with CFS (CDC 1994 criteria); 14-day sleep diary; momentary assessments; Chalder, Epworth, Trail Making Test, Cognitive Failures Questionnaire and HADS scales; hierarchical regressions.
hallazgos: Shorter time since diagnosis, more depression and more wake after sleep onset explained 23.4% of the variance in fatigue; male sex, depression and evening naps, 25.6% of objective cognitive dysfunction; anxiety, depression and morning naps, 32.2% of subjective. Long or evening naps were associated with greater sleepiness.
conclusion: Naps, especially in the afternoon, are associated with poorer cognitive functioning and more daytime sleepiness in CFS, with implications for symptom management.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions agree with those of the abstract (followed by introduction text). The role of depression and anxiety, highlighted in the results, does not appear in the keywords.

tema: Proposes a common European approach to investigating the economic impact of ME/CFS.
diseno: EUROMENE consensus methodological report; no primary data.
hallazgos: The economic burden appears large, mainly due to lost productivity. Studies are hampered by arbitrary case definitions, underdiagnosis and lack of prevalence data. Recommends Fukuda and CCC criteria, a common symptom list, prevalence-based cost-of-illness studies, PPP and EQ-5D.
conclusion: Formulates recommendations on case definition, identification, epidemiology and economic methods; the relationship between severity and economic impact should be a priority.
triangulacion: High coherence among the three sources; the PDF conclusions add the variation of costs according to severity and the heterogeneity of health systems.

tema: Editorial reviewing the epigenetic landscape of ME/CFS and its usefulness for deciphering complex phenotypes and patient subtypes.
diseno: Editorial / narrative review based on previous DNA methylation studies; no own population stated.
hallazgos: Preliminary DNA methylation examinations provide evidence of an important immune component and of distinct profiles between patient groups; increased expression of HDAC and miRNAs related to cell cycle and immune regulation are also mentioned.
conclusion: Mechanistic research is needed on how epigenetic modifications affect function and whether they are reversible, together with deep phenotyping, integration of biological and clinical data and study of histone and RNA marks to validate biomarkers.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract (which includes the editorial header and the start of the text) and PDF conclusions are consistent on methylation, immune component and phenotypes; the conclusions add the HPA axis and the comparison with related diseases such as fibromyalgia.

tema: Proposes the IDO metabolic trap hypothesis as the aetiology of ME/CFS, formulated as a mathematical model.
diseno: Database search for common deleterious mutations in human enzymes and mathematical model of tryptophan metabolism (IDO1, IDO2, LAT1 transporter).
hallazgos: 208 candidates were found, including IDO2 with four mutations. The model shows physiological and pathological steady states, with a critical point of cytosolic tryptophan beyond which the transition to the pathological state is inevitable; leaving it requires an external perturbation.
conclusion: If cytosolic tryptophan can be reduced below the critical point, the normal state would be recovered; the hypothesis can be tested with labelled tryptophan and tracer kinetics.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent. The conclusions text is only noise (contributions, funding, acknowledgements), so the conclusion comes from the abstract.

tema: Compares the characteristics of idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), fibromyalgia and CFS and links them to a common pathophysiology: increased CSF pressure.
diseno: Literature review contrasting the three conditions with the elevated cerebrospinal pressure hypothesis.
hallazgos: Shared characteristics attributable to elevated intracranial pressure include headache, fatigue, cognitive impairment, grey matter loss, cranial nerve involvement and overload of the olfactory lymphatic pathway; spinal pressure would explain diffuse pain, weakness, ataxia and sphincter symptoms. All three are associated with sympathetic hyperactivity, obesity, female predominance and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
conclusion: IIH, fibromyalgia and CFS probably share a disorder of elevated cerebrospinal pressure and could be considered progressive neurological disorders; research should focus on strategies to reduce CSF pressure.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are more assertive ('probably caused') and extend the hypothesis to other overlapping chronic pain conditions.

tema: Proposes a natural history framework for ME/CFS that integrates health determinants and the temporal variation of pathophysiology and phenotype.
diseno: Conceptual article based on literature, with preliminary UK ME/CFS Biobank data on cytokines and symptoms by disease duration.
hallazgos: Describes stages from asymptomatic predisposition and prodrome to symptomatic disease, with an initial neuroimmune and hypermetabolic state that may evolve into a hypometabolic one of low energy production, with possible reversion to milder states.
conclusion: No diagnostic criterion or molecular feature represents all patients at all stages; applying this framework could clarify mechanisms and identify therapeutic targets by stage.
triangulacion: Keywords (natural history, staging, prodrome), abstract and PDF conclusions agree; the conclusions mention the preliminary biobank data and acknowledge the limitations of the evidence.

tema: Investigates whether hypercoagulability, platelet hyperactivation and fibrinaloid microclots described in long COVID are present in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study in ME/CFS patients and healthy controls matched for sex and age (sample size not stated, described as low); thromboelastography in whole blood and platelet-poor plasma; fluorescence microscopy of microclots; platelet markers PAC-1 and CD62P.
hallazgos: The ME/CFS samples showed significant hypercoagulability; the area with fibrinaloid microclots was often more than 10 times greater than in controls, and platelets were hyperactivated (spreading score 2.72 ± 1.24 versus 1.00). The microclot load was lower than in long COVID.
conclusion: ME/CFS is accompanied by measurable changes in coagulability, platelet hyperactivation and microclots, pointing to systemic vascular pathology and endothelial inflammation; larger studies and caution regarding anticoagulation are required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are more cautious than the abstract, acknowledging the low number of participants and the need for corroboration before applying therapies.

tema: Explores the hypothesis that neuroglial dysfunction (astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes) is the common denominator of the pathobiology of ME/CFS.
diseno: Hypothesis-oriented review analysing the two most accepted features of ME/CFS: PEM and decreased cerebral blood flow. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Links PEM and the reduction in cerebral blood flow with dysfunctional or reactive neuroglia, which regulates autonomic functions, the immune system and the stress response.
conclusion: The multifaceted pathobiology of ME/CFS could be attributed in a unified way to neuroglial dysfunction, with relevance also for long COVID (PASC); greater focus on neuroglia is proposed.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent; the discussion acknowledges that the review rests partly on hypotheses still to be confirmed, something less explicit in the abstract, and includes funding noise.

tema: Suggests that dysfunction of ocular and ENT mucins could contribute to ME/CFS symptoms.
diseno: Hypothesis based on genetic analysis and computational modelling (logic model), with subjects recruited at a Miami veterans' centre; sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Mucins form the mucous layers that defend against pathogens; their alteration would prevent adequate mucosae from forming in ocular and ENT pathways, favouring chronic low-grade inflammation (rhinitis, dry eye, sore throat).
conclusion: The authors hypothesize that mucin dysfunction contributes to chronic inflammation and to the exacerbation of symptoms in ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the discussion text contains only ethical declarations, funding and contributions, with no conclusions, so the hypothesis rests on the abstract.

tema: Explains the social lack of awareness of CFS/ME through Pierre Bourdieu's theory of symbolic violence.
diseno: Qualitative and quantitative analysis (multiple correspondence analysis and hierarchical cluster) of patients' letters to the editor in three Spanish newspapers; number of letters not stated.
hallazgos: 13 mechanisms of symbolic violence were identified (non-recognition, institutionalized neglect, condescension, delegitimization, silencing, invisibilization, self-blame, among others); structural ones combine with symbolic ones.
conclusion: The mechanisms of symbolic violence offer a preliminary answer to why CFS is so little known; the role of gender, since it mainly affects women, will be central in future studies.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree; the abstract has no explicit conclusion and the conclusions (discussion, with acknowledgement noise) add the gender axis, absent from the keywords.
